pros: Near-constant time per operation: amortized O(α(V))
Extremely memory-efficient: only two arrays (parent and rank)
Simple to implement with clear logic
Provably optimal for pointer-based disjoint set representations
Path compression makes repeated finds essentially free
Union by rank guarantees logarithmic tree height
Widely applicable across graph algorithms and beyond
Both optimizations together achieve the α(V) bound
Can be extended to track additional per-set information
cons: Does not support edge deletion (decremental operations)
Path compression uses recursion (stack overflow risk in naive impl)
Iterative path compression is slightly more complex
Cannot efficiently enumerate elements of a set
α(V) bound only holds for amortized analysis, not per-operation
Initial construction is O(V) (must initialize all elements)
Requires integer element indices (0 to V-1) for optimal performance
Union by size uses different logic than union by rank
Not suitable for graphs with frequent splits
